author: NorthEast News Desk
body: NH Chronicle is marking a half-century of mud football in the Mount Washington Valley with a new retrospective on the Hogs, the local team whose name became closely tied to the region’s unusual athletic tradition.

WMUR’s program brings members of the group back together and traces how playing football in mud grew into a recognizable North Conway event. The setting became known as Hog Coliseum, behind the community center in the village.

The story is less about conventional standings than about the people who kept returning to the field and built a durable community identity around the game. The reunion gives former participants a chance to connect the early years with the tradition remembered by later spectators.

For the Mount Washington Valley, the retrospective also preserves a piece of local culture that sits outside the area’s familiar skiing and hiking image. A 50-year run turns what began as a novelty into community history, and WMUR’s account records the people behind it while those memories can still be shared firsthand.
dek: A new WMUR retrospective reunites members of the Hogs and looks back at a muddy football tradition rooted in North Conway.
headline: NH Chronicle revisits 50-year Mud Bowl tradition in Mount Washington Valley
